title: Mr. Robinson, the garage owner behind Local 767
summary: The older mechanic whose garage housed the union acted as secretary.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: One other question -- do you remember who the musician was whose garage 767 was in?
His name was Robinson. He was primarily an automotive mechanic. And he was an older fellow. And as
I said, they didn't have money enough to hire a hall or have a place of their own, so this old man was just good enough to allow them to use the back room of his garage.
Did he play an instrument with your group?
I don't remember whether he played anything or not.
I, I wasn't necessarily a part of the union --
He was -- I think he was secretary. He worked -- not worked, but he acted as secretary. I think Mr. Robinson was secretary. I was too young at the game to pay any attention to that side of it.
